input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Section (h) is the assignment clause and it meets our preferred position on the material terms: we may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. There is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the Agreement, so the Vendor has no termination or re-pricing right on our change of control (the only termination triggers are insolvency-type events in p0016-p0017). Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express bar on Vendor assigning to a competitor of ours, and the affiliate/successor carve-out is mutual rather than one-way in our favour. Neither is material, and the mutuality is consistent with the fallback position in any event.
